section: President of India - election, qualifications, term, impeachment; executive, legislative, financial, judicial powers
subsections: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

accepted.s: Under Article 54 of the Constitution of India, which one of the following is included in the electoral college for the election of the President?
o: Nominated members of the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry
Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry
Nominated members of both Houses of Parliament
Elected members of the Legislative Councils of the States
accepted.x: The electoral college includes elected MPs and elected MLAs of the States, Delhi and Puducherry. Nominated members and members of Legislative Councils are excluded.
accepted.tq: Distinguish elected members of eligible Houses from nominated members and Legislative Council members.
accepted.sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

accepted.s: A Chief Minister who is a member of the Legislative Council of a State, rather than its Legislative Assembly, is entitled to
o: not vote in the election of the President
vote only if nominated by the Governor
vote in the election of the President by virtue of being the Chief Minister
vote only in the election of the Vice-President
accepted.x: Only elected members of State Legislative Assemblies form part of the Presidential electoral college. Membership of a Legislative Council does not confer this right, even on a Chief Minister.
accepted.tq: Apply the precise constitutional distinction between the Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council.
accepted.sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the electoral college for the election of the President:
1. Nominated members of both Houses of Parliament are excluded.
2. Members of State Legislative Councils are excluded.
3. Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry are included.
4. Elected members of all Union Territory Legislative Assemblies are included.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the Constitution specifically includes Delhi and Puducherry, while Union Territories without Assemblies do not participate.
accepted.tq: Find the overbroad statement by separating the named Union Territories from all other Union Territories.
accepted.sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

accepted.s: The election of the President of India is held by
o: direct voting through universal adult franchise and open ballot
simple majority voting by elected MPs and MLAs
proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and open ballot
proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and secret ballot
accepted.x: Article 55(3) prescribes proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and voting by secret ballot.
accepted.tq: Test the paired constitutional features together: STV and secret ballot.
accepted.sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

accepted.s: The system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote used in the election of the President was borrowed from the Constitution of
o: South Africa
Canada
Australia
Ireland
accepted.x: The Presidential election method of proportional representation by single transferable vote was borrowed from Ireland.
accepted.tq: Use the source-country association for a distinctive constitutional device.
accepted.sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

accepted.s: The constitutional objective of maintaining uniformity among the States and parity between the States as a whole and the Union in the Presidential election is secured through
o: direct election by the people of India
equal vote value for every elector irrespective of the House represented
nomination of an equal number of electors by every State
differential value assigned to MLA and MP votes
accepted.x: Article 55(1) achieves these principles by assigning vote values to MLAs based on State population and distributing the aggregate MLA vote value among elected MPs.
accepted.tq: Connect the constitutional objective with the mechanism that gives effect to it.
accepted.sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

accepted.s: The value of the vote of an elected member of a State Legislative Assembly is calculated by the formula:
o: Number of elected MLAs divided by State population, multiplied by 1,000
State population divided by the number of elected MLAs, multiplied by 1/1,000
State population divided by the number of elected MLAs, multiplied by 1,000
State population divided by the total number of members of both Houses of Parliament
accepted.x: The value of an MLA's vote is calculated as (population of the State divided by the number of elected MLAs) multiplied by 1/1000.
accepted.tq: Read the formula carefully and distinguish multiplication by 1/1000 from multiplication by 1000.
accepted.sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

accepted.s: The value of the vote of an elected Member of Parliament in the election of the President is determined by
o: multiplying the value of the highest-valued MLA vote by the number of States
dividing the total value of all MLA votes by the total number of elected MPs
dividing the total number of elected MPs by the total value of all MLA votes
assigning an identical value fixed by Parliament to every MP
accepted.x: The value of an MP's vote equals the total value of all votes of elected MLAs divided by the total number of elected MPs.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct numerator and denominator in the constitutional calculation.
accepted.sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

accepted.s: For determining the value of votes in the Presidential election, the population of the States is presently taken on the basis of the
o: 1981 Census
1961 Census
1971 Census
2011 Census
accepted.x: The population base for calculating the value of votes is the 1971 Census, which has been frozen for this purpose.
accepted.tq: Test the frozen census base rather than the latest available census.
accepted.sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

accepted.s: The population base used for calculating the value of votes in the Presidential election is to remain frozen until
o: the first Census conducted after 2021
the first Census conducted after 2026
a constitutional amendment made after every Census
the first Census conducted after 2031
accepted.x: The 1971 Census base remains frozen until the first Census conducted after 2026, as provided through the constitutional arrangement referred to in the 84th Amendment.
accepted.tq: Use the end-point of a constitutional freeze instead of substituting a recent census year.
accepted.sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional position regarding disputes connected with the election of the President?
o: They are decided by the Election Commission of India alone.
They are decided by Parliament through a joint sitting.
They are decided by the Council of Ministers.
They are decided only by the Supreme Court.
accepted.x: Under Article 71, disputes relating to the election of the President are decided only by the Supreme Court.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional dispute with the authority expressly entrusted to decide it.
accepted.sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

accepted.s: If the election of the President is subsequently declared void, which one of the following is the effect on acts performed by the President before such declaration?
o: Such acts remain valid.
All such acts automatically become void.
Their validity is decided by the outgoing President.
Only financial acts remain valid; all other acts become void.
accepted.x: Article 71 protects acts done by the President in the performance of duties before the election is declared void; those acts do not become invalid merely because of the declaration.
accepted.tq: Separate the validity of past official acts from the validity of the election itself.
accepted.sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

accepted.s: A vacancy in the electoral college for the election of the President
o: does not by itself constitute a ground for challenging the election
can be challenged only if caused by resignation of an MP
requires postponement of the election until the vacancy is filled
automatically invalidates the election
accepted.x: Article 71(4) provides that the election of the President cannot be called in question on the ground of any vacancy in the electoral college.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional exception that prevents a vacancy from defeating the election.
accepted.sec: Electoral college - who votes, who does not, value of vote

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Article)
A. Article 52
B. Article 54
C. Article 60
D. Article 71

List-II (Subject)
1. Oath or affirmation of the President
2. Election disputes
3. There shall be a President of India
4. Electoral college for election of the President
accepted.x: Article 52 provides for the office of the President, Article 54 concerns the electoral college, Article 60 concerns the oath or affirmation, and Article 71 concerns election disputes.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure article-subject pairs and eliminate codes with a misplaced constitutional provision.
accepted.sec: Articles 52-62 number game

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 57 — Eligibility for re-election
Article 56 — Term of office of the President
Article 59 — Conditions of the President's office
Article 62 — Oath or affirmation of the President
accepted.x: Article 62 deals with the time of election to fill a vacancy in the office of the President. The oath or affirmation is dealt with by Article 60.
accepted.tq: Find the single article-subject swap among closely placed provisions.
accepted.sec: Articles 52-62 number game

accepted.s: The constitutional provision relating to the impeachment of the President of India is contained in Article
accepted.x: Article 61 lays down the procedure for impeachment of the President.
accepted.tq: Use the article-number sequence and distinguish impeachment from qualifications, conditions and vacancy.
accepted.sec: Articles 52-62 number game

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 53 vests the executive power of the Union in the President.
2. Article 56 deals with the term of office of the President and resignation to the Vice-President.
3. Article 58 lays down the qualifications for election as President.
4. Article 60 deals with the President's eligibility for re-election.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false: Article 60 concerns the oath or affirmation, while eligibility for re-election is dealt with by Article 57.
accepted.tq: Catch the adjacent-article substitution between re-election and oath provisions.
accepted.sec: Articles 52-62 number game

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the sequence of subjects covered by Articles 52, 53, 54 and 55?
o: President; executive power; election; manner of election
Executive power; President; manner of election; election disputes
President; election; executive power; impeachment
Qualifications; executive power; election; term of office
accepted.x: Article 52 provides for the President, Article 53 vests Union executive power in the President, Article 54 concerns the electoral college, and Article 55 prescribes the manner of election.
accepted.tq: Follow the consecutive article sequence from the office itself to its election method.
accepted.sec: Articles 52-62 number game

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 65 — Vice-President to act as President
Article 72 — Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President
Article 74 — President's power of pardon
Article 78 — Attorney General of India
accepted.x: Article 65 provides for the Vice-President acting as President in specified circumstances. Article 72 concerns pardon, Article 74 concerns aid and advice by the Council of Ministers, and Article 76 concerns the Attorney General.
accepted.tq: Use neighbouring constitutional provisions as distractors and identify the exact article-subject pairing.
accepted.sec: Articles 52-62 number game

accepted.s: Articles 52 to 78 of the Constitution of India constitute
o: Part V, Chapter I dealing with the Union Executive
Part VI, Chapter I dealing with the State Executive
Part III dealing with Fundamental Rights
Part V, Chapter II dealing with Parliament
accepted.x: Articles 52 to 78 fall under Part V, Chapter I, which deals with the Union Executive.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Part and Chapter classification from the adjacent chapter on Parliament.
accepted.sec: Articles 52-62 number game

accepted.s:
Which of the following are legislative functions of the President of India?
1. Summoning and proroguing both Houses of Parliament
2. Dissolving the Lok Sabha
3. Summoning a joint sitting of Parliament
4. Sending messages to either House of Parliament
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: The President can summon and prorogue Parliament, dissolve the Lok Sabha, summon a joint sitting, and send messages to either House. A joint sitting is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
accepted.tq: Check whether all listed functions belong to the President's legislative field rather than treating the joint sitting as a parliamentary initiative alone.
accepted.sec: Articles 52-62 number game

accepted.s: The President addresses Parliament under Articles 86 and 87 on, among other occasions,
o: every session before the presentation of the Union Budget
only the last session of every year
only a joint sitting convened during a constitutional emergency
the first session after each general election and the first session of each year
accepted.x: The President addresses both Houses assembled together at the first session after each general election and at the first session of each year under Articles 86 and 87.
accepted.tq: Distinguish constitutionally specified occasions from routine parliamentary sessions.
accepted.sec: Articles 52-62 number game

accepted.s: A Bill passed by Parliament cannot become law unless it receives the assent of the President because
o: the President is not a component of Parliament
the President is a part of Parliament under Article 79
the President alone introduces every Bill in Parliament
the President presides over both Houses of Parliament
accepted.x: Article 79 makes the President a part of Parliament. Consequently, a Bill passed by Parliament requires Presidential assent to become law.
accepted.tq: Link the constitutional composition of Parliament with the assent requirement.
accepted.sec: Articles 52-62 number game

accepted.s:
Under Article 240, the President may make regulations for which of the following Union Territories?
1. Andaman and Nicobar Islands
2. Lakshadweep
3. Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
4. Puducherry when its Legislative Assembly is suspended or dissolved
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1, 2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: Article 240 covers the listed Union Territories, including Puducherry when its Legislative Assembly is suspended or dissolved. The President administers Union Territories through administrators.
accepted.tq: Test the complete territorial list and the special condition attached to Puducherry.
accepted.sec: Articles 52-62 number game
